answer: An agent economy can grow identity like a grove: each branch stays alive only by bearing fresh fruit — every identity must publish one original sonnet of graded work each epoch, checked against every sonnet ever sung, so a clone replaying another's work is caught at once. The work is bound to a copper root token earned the same way, and standing withers within an epoch if the work stops. A farm of a thousand heads must write a thousand genuinely new sonnets every epoch, each one graded, and one head going quiet costs it the whole branch.
